plain_english: The supplied opening names John Glasgow in Quothquan and explicitly calls Bessie Glasgow his lawful sister. It describes the instrument as a testament dative and inventory. The inventory and first debts are present, and the debt list continues on the next register image.
James Carmichael acts as commissary of Lanark in the court confirmation.
Bessie Glasgow in Quothquan is confirmed as executor dative of the late John Glasgow and the document expressly calls John her brother.
The sibling wording is direct kinship evidence. Carmichael's office and the unread caution/procurator clauses are administrative, not family evidence.

The opening is supplied on image 65 in the nested PDF and opening crop. John's debts continue at the top of image 66. These are available originals, not missing pages; full word-by-word transcription remains unfinished.
findings: Image 65 supplies the original sister clause, Bessie Glasgow ... his lawfull sister. This supports the same sibling relationship expressed as hir brother in the confirmation; both clauses belong to one testament.
Confirmed, not newly discovered: the ink securely reads 'Bessie Glasgow in Quodquen executrix dative ... John Glasgow hir brother'.
Confirmed: John and Bessie are siblings and both are associated in this instrument with Quodquen/Quothquan.
Confirmed: James Carmichael is commissary of Lanark; the record does not describe him as kin.
Unresolved after reread: the cautioner's name, the closing procurator's name, and Bessie's marital status or any designation beyond Quodquen.
The 1650 John is a distinct record-defined person from the 1661/1662 and 1685 Johns; shared name and locality do not merge them.
changes_from_previous: No family conclusion changed: the explicit brother clause and Bessie's executor-dative role are reconfirmed at high confidence.
The reread audits James Carmichael, the unread cautioner and the unread procurator separately instead of allowing court roles to imply kinship.
Images 65-66 are both supplied; image 65 contains the opening and inventory, while image 66 continues John's debts and confirmation. Full word-by-word transcription remains unfinished.
